## Description

Monitor public SEC Schedule 13D filings and amendments, parse the filer, target, ownership stake, stated purpose, campaign demands, and filing novelty, then rank events using target liquidity, valuation, prior returns, and the observed post-publication price reaction. Only act on information available at or after the public filing; consider skipping events where the price has already repriced or liquidity is inadequate.

## Where it may fit

Discrete corporate-event opportunities; dependent on filing flow and market reaction rather than a continuous market-regime signal.

## Vehicles

U.S.-listed common stocks with adequate liquidity; long-only event portfolio or watchlist.

## Required data

SEC EDGAR Schedule 13D/13D-A filing text and timestamps, security identifiers, point-in-time prices and volume, fundamentals, corporate-action data, spread/slippage estimates, and event calendars.

## Caveats

A large fraction of reported event-window price movement may occur before or around disclosure, so published announcement returns are not a post-filing strategy return estimate. Separate filing date from underlying transaction date, avoid look-ahead leakage, account for overnight gaps and spreads, and use only public information. The exact screening and execution rules must be tested.
